incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service=inference-runtime severity=sev2 pager=oncall-team triggered by 3xx -> 5xx ratio spike (90s window) — page_id=pg_1799009876
Maya (oncall): I’m on it. seeing elevated 5xx across /v1/generate on two AZs. triaging now.
Liam (eng-runtime): thanks @Maya. initial thought: KV cache eviction storm or routing fallback to slow model. can you dump top error types?
Maya (oncall): logs show lots of `kv cache miss -> model reload` followed by `grpc deadline exceeded` and `OOM` in a few pods. attaching quick snippets:
```
[2026-03-15T18:24:02Z] inference-runtime pod-12 - ERROR - kv_cache: eviction threshold hit, reshuffle start
[2026-03-15T18:24:03Z] inference-runtime pod-12 - ERROR - model-loader: reload failed: OOM while allocating 2.1GB
[2026-03-15T18:24:03Z] inference-runtime pod-14 - WARN - request timed out: grpc deadline exceeded
```
Liam (eng-runtime): ok that matches a cold-start cascade. did autoscaler spin up new nodes? might have raced with scheduling.
Diego (infra): Autoscaler reports burst scale events at 18:23:58, but node provisioning latencies were ~45s due to transient spot capacity shortage in us-west-2.
Esther (sre): customer-facing impact? any errors tied to a specific customer or route?
Maya (oncall): about ~12% of requests failed with 5xx in that 5-minute interval. Mostly hosted API but some Dedicated pools saw retries. I’ve flagged customer-facing routes: `/v1/generate` and `/v1/chat`.
Anna (product): Heads up: a customer reported rate-limited errors in-app around 18:25. I'm drafting a comms note.
Sam (sre): Live mitigation idea: temporarily route traffic away from the two affected AZs to healthy pools and enable a short-lived 429-backoff at the edge to reduce retry storm. @Diego can you run a quick shift of weight?
Diego (infra): starting rollout of routing change: moving 30% of traffic off us-west-2 to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 via traffic-policy rule `reduce-weight-us-west-2`. ETA 40s.
ops-bot: deploy started by Diego (infra) — change_id=chg_1799009876_1 status=IN_PROGRESS
Maya (oncall): after routing change, 5xx rate down to 3% within 90s. Good sign.
Liam (eng-runtime): also enabling aggressive KV cache warmup: prefetch top-10 models on new pods, and temporarily disable model reloads older than 2 minutes to avoid OOM thrash. Pushing runtime flag `--prefetch=true --reload-cooldown=120s`.
Sam (sre): adding a short-term alert suppression on the noisy `kv_eviction` rule so we don't page repeatedly while we stabilize. suppression window 15m.
ops-bot: change applied — change_id=chg_1799009876_1 status=COMPLETE
Diego (infra): routing change complete. traffic distribution: us-east-1 45%, eu-west-1 25%, us-west-2 30%.
Maya (oncall): 5xx spike settled, error rate back to baseline 0.6% after ~7 minutes. Moving to post-incident triage.
Liam (eng-runtime): quick notes for postmortem: root cause appears to be spot capacity shortfall causing slow node provisioning -> cache cold starts -> model reload OOMs -> retry cascade. Contributing factor: paging noise and the autoscaler not marking in-flight provisioning as "safety headroom" for persistent pools.
Esther (sre): I’ll create the postmortem doc. suggested timeline: prep draft by EOD, postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00am PST.
Anna (product): Requesting customer impact summary for the comms. Maya can you capture affected customer IDs and approximate error windows?
Maya (oncall): captured affected customer orgs: [acme-saas, betaapps, partner-x]. errors ranged 18:23:50 - 18:31:10. Estimated requests affected: ~12k.
Sam (sre): action items we should track in the postmortem: 
1) Autoscaler: add capacity reservation for Dedicated pools and prefer on-demand fallback for critical model loads — owner: Diego — due: 2026-03-22
2) Inference runtime: default `reload-cooldown` and prefetch heuristics for new nodes, and hard OOM guards to reject rather than crash — owner: Liam — due: 2026-03-19
3) Alerting: introduce a three-stage paging rule for `kv_eviction` (info -> slack only -> pager) with dynamic suppression during scaling events — owner: Esther — due: 2026-03-18
4) Observability: add a `model_reload` trace and dashboard with percent-of-requests impacted and tail-latency by AZ — owner: Sam — due: 2026-03-20
5) Customer comms: finalize and send incident summary + SLO credits proposal — owner: Anna — due: 2026-03-16
Esther (sre): I’m creating the postmortem doc now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/IR-1799009876 (draft)
Maya (oncall): note for oncall playbooks: add a step to consider immediate traffic-weight shifts and 429-backoff when large-scale `kv cache miss` pattern is detected.
Liam (eng-runtime): sample alert query we should review (Datadog-ish pseudo):
```
avg(last_1m):sum:inference.kv_eviction{env:prod,service:inference-runtime} by {az} > 50
```
Proposed improved alert: add a derivative and correlate with node_provisioning_time and model_reload_rate to avoid false positives during planned scaling.
```
(derivative(sum:inference.kv_eviction{*}.rollup(sum,60)) > 10) AND (avg:cloud.node.provisioning_time{*} > 20)
```
Diego (infra): for the autoscaler change I propose: when provisioning from spot, automatically reserve a small on-demand headroom threshold (config `spot_fallback_headroom_pct=10`) for inference-critical pools.
Anna (product): Product asks for SLO impact calc: if 12k requests failed out of 1.5M total in the window, that’s ~0.8% availability hit for that minute. We need to standardize how we compute SLO credits.
Sam (sre): Estimating customer exposure matrix and draft SLO credit calc in the PM doc.
Esther (sre): scheduling postmortem meeting: tomorrow 10:00-10:45 (PST). please add to calendar if you’re an owner.
Maya (oncall): quick wins to apply before postmortem: 1) keep the suppression on `kv_eviction` for 15m, 2) set runtime `reload-cooldown` to 120s on canary to validate, 3) pre-warm most common model shards on scale events. I’ll coordinate with Liam & Diego.
Liam (eng-runtime): doing canary push of `--reload-cooldown=120s` to 10% fleet now.
ops-bot: canary deploy started — deploy_id=deploy_1799009876_canary status=IN_PROGRESS
Liam (eng-runtime): canary reports: no regressions after 12 minutes. CPU and memory stable.
ops-bot: canary deploy complete — deploy_id=deploy_1799009876_canary status=COMPLETE
Diego (infra): I submitted an RFC for spot fallback headroom and a guardian flag for Dedicated pools: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RF-425 (draft).
Sam (sre): creating an alert-rule PR to add the 3-stage paging: https://git.redwood/sre/alerts/pulls/312 — please review @Esther @Liam
Anna (product): I’ll ship a short customer note and triple-check Dedicated customers for any SLA exposure.
Maya (oncall): thanks everyone. marking incident resolved in the thread and moving to postmortem follow-up.
